name: Underground Resistance
hook: A second-generation Detroit collective who ran techno as a political project, in ski masks, against major labels and the artists who signed to them.

blurb.age7: Underground Resistance was a group of Detroit musicians who made angry, powerful techno music and refused to hide who they were making it for.
blurb.age13: Founded in 1989 by Mike Banks, Jeff Mills, and Robert Hood, Underground Resistance rejected the major-label deals some of the first Detroit techno artists had signed. They performed and released records anonymously, in masks and combat gear, treating techno as a tool for political and economic self-determination rather than a genre to be sold off.
blurb.adult: UR positioned itself explicitly against the commercialization the first-wave Belleville Three artists had begun to accept, tying that stance to the same Reagan-era Detroit economic collapse the earlier scene had already made central to its identity. The group operated as both a production unit and an independent label, refusing distribution deals that would cede control of the masters, a direct response to the labels overlay running through this dataset.
